text:
296
Berlin den 8. Xbr.
1815
verehrtesten Freund
Was alhier bei mir eingelaufen ist, für
ge ich bei: der Hoffrath Bar¬
by ist in Paris gestorben,
ich will bei der Witwe auch
noch nach fragen. Der Staats
kanzler wird diese Woche
erwartet. Philippischen
soll in Stache[?] sehr krank
geworden seyn, welches mir
innigst nahm gehet. Auch
Deiner Krankheit wegen sey
meiner Theilnahme ver¬
sichert. Ich erwarte doch recht
bald.
Cosmar
ist in er¬
ei[?] Instanz
eines un¬
redlichen
verfahrens über¬
führ geachtet — hat
aber appellirt. bleibt es
dabei, so verliert er die
vormundschaft.
Dein
treu geh. diener
Grevenitz
Gestern etc. der H. Staats Kanzler
wirklich angelangt —  dieses
melde ich sogleich unter Bei fü¬
gung der 2 Original Anlagen
Philippischen soll jezt ihn
fährlich krank seyn — mein
Schmerz ist so gros als wäre
es meine eigne Kohler[?]
dein
tr[eu]. geh.
Grevenitz
8 Xbr. 1815.

translation.en:
296 Berlin, the 8th of December 1815. Most esteemed Friend, What has come in here to me I enclose herewith: the Court Councillor Barby has died in Paris; I mean to enquire further of the widow as well. The State Chancellor is expected this week. Philippischen is said to have fallen very ill at Stache[?], which touches me most deeply. Be assured also of my sympathy on account of your illness. I do indeed expect [you/it] very soon.

Cosmar

has at first instance[?]

been held convicted of a dishonest proceeding — but has appealed. If it stands so, he loses the guardianship.

Your faithful and obedient servant, Grevenitz

Yesterday, etc., the State Chancellor really arrived — this I report at once, with the 2 original enclosures appended. Philippischen is said now to be dangerously ill — my grief is as great as if it were my own Kohler[?]. Your

faithful and obedient,

Grevenitz

8 December 1815.

The State Chancellor is expected this week. Philippischen is said to have fallen very ill at Stache[?], which touches me most deeply. Be assured also of my sympathy on account of your illness. I do indeed expect [you/it] very soon.

Cosmar

has at first instance[?]

been held convicted of a dishonest proceeding — but has appealed. If it stands so, he loses the guardianship.

Your faithful and obedient servant, Grevenitz

faithful and obedient,

Grevenitz

8 December 1815.
summary_en: Grevenitz sends Triebenfeld the post that has reached him together with two original enclosures. He reports that Court Councillor Barby has died in Paris and says he intends to make enquiries with the widow. The State Chancellor had been expected and has meanwhile arrived. Philippischen is said to be dangerously ill. Grevenitz expresses his sympathy over Triebenfeld's illness. Cosmar, he says, has been convicted of dishonest dealing in the first instance but has appealed; should that stand, he will lose the guardianship.
summary_de: Grevenitz schickt Triebenfeld die bei ihm eingegangene Post und zwei Original-Anlagen. Er meldet, dass Hoffrath Barby in Paris gestorben ist, und will bei der Witwe nachfragen. Der Staats Kanzler wurde erwartet und ist inzwischen angekommen. Philippischen soll gefährlich krank sein. Grevenitz bekundet Anteil an Triebenfelds Krankheit. Cosmar wurde in erster Instanz unredlichen Verfahrens überführt, hat aber appelliert; bleibt es dabei, verliert er die Vormundschaft.

reading.notes: Grevenitz writes from Berlin to Triebenfeld, addressed as a friend. He encloses post that has come for Triebenfeld and reports that Hoffrath Barby (probably Barbe, whose death is also reported in doc. 297) has died in Paris; he will ask the widow. The Staats Kanzler is expected this week, and a postscript says he arrived yesterday. Two original enclosures are sent. Philippischen is said to be seriously ill. Grevenitz sends sympathy on Triebenfeld's own illness. Cosmar has been found guilty at first instance of dishonest dealing and has appealed; if the verdict stands he loses the guardianship. The letter has nothing on Trąbczyn.
